title: Nouns 3: Making Plurals with -ы and -и
description: Most Russian plurals are formed by swapping the singular ending for -ы or -и. The choice between them is governed by a small but powerful orthographic rule (the seven-letter rule): after Г, К, Х and Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч, Russian never writes -ы; it always writes -и.
descriptionRussian: Большинство русских существительных образуют множественное число, меняя окончание на -ы или -и. Выбор между ними определяется небольшим, но очень важным орфографическим правилом — правилом семи букв: после Г, К, Х и Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч русский язык никогда не пишет -ы, всегда -и.
intro: Making a Russian noun plural is mostly a matter of swapping one ending for another, and two endings do the bulk of the work. What makes this lesson worth slowing down for is the spelling rule that sits on top of them. It decides which of the two you write, it overrides the default every time, and it will follow you into adjectives, cases, and verbs for the rest of your Russian. Learn it cleanly here and you stop paying for it later.
rules: The dominant Russian plural is formed by swapping the singular ending for -ы or -и. The basic default: hard endings (masculine + nothing, feminine -а) → -ы; soft endings (-й, -ь, -я) → -и.
The seven-letter rule (правило семи букв): after the letters Г, К, Х and Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч, Russian never writes -ы. It always writes -и. This rule is absolute and applies far beyond plurals.
Masculine plurals: hard consonant → -ы (журнал → журналы); after Г/К/Х (ученик) or Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч (нож, врач) → -и (ученики, ножи, врачи); -й → -и (музей → музеи); -ь → -и (словарь → словари).
Feminine plurals: -а → -ы (машина → машины); -а after Г/К/Х (книга, ёлка) or Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч (девушка) → -и (книги, ёлки, девушки); -я → -и (неделя → недели); -ь → -и (ночь → ночи).
The choice between -ы and -и is made by the stem-final consonant, not by the noun's gender. Both ученик (M) and книга (F) take -и because the stem ends in one of the seven letters.
examples: журнал → журналы. (M, hard -л + -ы, no spelling rule fires.)
ученик → ученики. (M, stem ends in к → -и by the seven-letter rule.)
словарь → словари. (M, soft -ь is replaced by -и.)
машина → машины. (F, hard -а replaced by -ы; the stem ends in н, not one of the seven letters.)
книга → книги. (F, stem ends in г → -и by the seven-letter rule, not the expected -ы.)
ночь → ночи. (F, soft -ь is replaced by -и; the stem also happens to end in ч, so the rule reinforces the soft pattern.)

tables.title: Russian Plurals: When to Write -ы and When to Write -и

rows.label: M: hard consonant (not Г/К/Х or Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч)
cells: журнал → журналы, стол → столы, телефон → телефоны

rows.label: M: stem ends in Г/К/Х or Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч
cells: ученик → ученики, нож → ножи, врач → врачи

rows.label: F: -а (stem not Г/К/Х or Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч)
cells: машина → машины, лампа → лампы, сестра → сёстры

rows.label: F: -а after Г/К/Х or Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч
cells: книга → книги, ёлка → ёлки, девушка → девушки

rows.label: F: -я
cells: неделя → недели, песня → песни, кухня → кухни

rows.label: F: -ь
cells: ночь → ночи, дверь → двери, тетрадь → тетради

items.hint: Hard consonant stem, no spelling rule fires. Use the default masculine plural.
items.explanation: Журнал ends in -л, a hard consonant that is NOT one of the seven letters. With no spelling rule blocking it, the default masculine plural -ы applies: журналы.

items.hint: What is the last letter of the stem? Does the seven-letter rule fire?
items.explanation: The stem of книга ends in г. After г, Russian never writes -ы (the seven-letter rule). The plural is книги.

items.hint: Soft sign -ь turns into what in the plural?
items.explanation: The soft sign -ь is replaced by -и in the plural: ночь → ночи. (As a bonus, the stem also ends in ч, one of the seven letters, so the spelling rule would forbid -ы anyway.)

items.hint: Ученик ends in к. What does the seven-letter rule say?
items.explanation: Ученик ends in -к. After к, Russian writes -и, never -ы. The plural is ученики. The subject of the sentence is in the nominative plural.

items.promptEnglish: My dictionaries are on the shelf.
items.explanation: The soft sign -ь is replaced by -и in the plural: словарь → словари.

items.hint: Feminine -я is replaced by what in the plural?
items.explanation: Feminine -я is replaced by -и in the plural: песня → песни. The accusative plural for inanimate nouns is the same as the nominative plural.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The stem of книга ends in г. After г, Russian never writes -ы (the seven-letter rule), so -и takes over: книги. Это always takes the plain (nominative) form, so the noun stays in the plural nominative.

errorCorrection.sentence: На полке лежат новые ручкы для урока.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There are new pens for the lesson on the shelf.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ручка's stem ends in -к. The seven-letter spelling rule blocks -ы after к/г/х/ж/ш/щ/ч, so the plural ending switches to -и: ручки. Ручкы is invalid Russian spelling, exactly the trap the rule exists to catch.

errorCorrection.sentence: Все мои рубль в этой сумке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: All my rubles are in this bag.
errorCorrection.explanation: Рубль is masculine soft-stem (-ь). The soft-stem plural takes -и: рубли. The construction 'Все мои X' requires plural X (both 'все' and 'мои' are plural).

errorCorrection.sentence: Русские ученикы читают сложный текст в библиотеке.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Russian students are reading a difficult text in the library.
errorCorrection.explanation: Ученик's stem ends in -к. The seven-letter rule blocks -ы after к, so the plural ending switches to -и: ученики. Ученикы is invalid Russian spelling: the same rule that produces книги from книга. The adjective 'русские' (plural) signals that the noun must be plural too.

patternRecognition.question: Which rule forces -и here, instead of the expected -ы?
patternRecognition.explanation: Without the seven-letter rule we would expect книгы (the default feminine -а → -ы swap). But the stem ends in г, one of the seven letters, so -ы is forbidden. The plural must be книги.

patternRecognition.question: Which rule picks -и here?
patternRecognition.explanation: Словарь ends in the soft sign -ь, which becomes -и in the plural. The seven-letter rule does not fire here (the stem ends in р, not one of the seven). The pick is made purely by the soft-sign pattern.

patternRecognition.question: Why does -ы win here, rather than -и?
options: Because the stem is hard and ends in none of the seven letters.
patternRecognition.answer: Because the stem is hard and ends in none of the seven letters.
patternRecognition.explanation: Журнал ends in -л, a hard consonant that is not among the seven (Г/К/Х/Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч). With no spelling rule blocking it, the default -ы applies. Plural: журналы.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each noun by which plural ending it takes. Check the last letter of the stem: if it is Г, К, Х, Ж, Ш, Щ, or Ч, the seven-letter rule forces -и.

reviewVocab.definition: after Г, К, Х and Ж, Ш, Щ, Ч, Russian never writes -ы; always -и. Applies far beyond plurals.
reviewVocab.example: Книга → книги. Ученик → ученики. Врач → врачи.

reviewVocab.definition: default: hard M + feminine -а → -ы; soft -й, -ь, -я → -и. The seven-letter rule overrides -ы after Г/К/Х/Ж/Ш/Щ/Ч.
reviewVocab.example: стол → столы, словарь → словари, книга → книги.

reviewVocab.definition: the consonant just before the singular ending. The seven-letter rule fires on this consonant, not on the gender of the noun.
reviewVocab.example: Журнал has -л (rule does not fire) → журналы. Книга has -г (rule fires) → книги.
